import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Target schema columns and types
    target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
    target_dtypes = {
        'admit': int,
        'gre': int,
        'gpa': float,
        'prestige': int
    }

    # Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and types
        df = df[target_columns].copy()
        df = df.astype(target_dtypes)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Since all sources have the same schema and represent similar data,
    # the transformation is a union of all source tables.
    # No additional join or aggregation is required based on the problem statement.

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
